title: Mixers, deviation and intermodulation
blurb: Explain what a mixer outputs, work out FM bandwidth and deviation, and know why odd-order intermodulation products land closest.

G8B01.why: Tuning the **local oscillator** changes which input frequency lands on the fixed IF.
G8B01.trap: The BFO is for SSB/CW detection and the image is a problem, not a control.

G8B02.why: A signal one IF on the far side of the LO also mixes to the IF: the **image**, twice the IF from the wanted signal.

G8B03.trap: Synthesizing generates frequencies, it doesn't mix two inputs.

G8B04.why: A **multiplier** generates a harmonic of a lower oscillator frequency to reach the operating frequency.
G8B04.trap: A mixer shifts frequency by adding or subtracting, it doesn't multiply.

G8B05.why: **Odd-order** products (2F1−F2, 2F2−F1) fall right beside the original signals. Even-order products land far away.

G8B06.trap: 8 kHz is only one side of the carrier.

G8B07.why: The oscillator frequency is multiplied 12 times (146.52 ÷ 12.21), so its deviation is 5 kHz ÷ 12 = **416.7 Hz**.

G8B08.why: High-duty modes transmit nearly continuously, so their **average power** can exceed the transmitter's average rating.

G8B09.why: A receiver bandwidth matched to the mode passes the whole signal and little noise: **best signal-to-noise ratio**.
G8B09.trap: It is a performance choice, not an FCC rule.

G8B10.why: Faster symbols are shorter pulses, which spread wider in frequency: **higher symbol rates need more bandwidth**.

G8B11.why: A mixer outputs the **sum and difference** of the LO and RF input frequencies.
G8B11.trap: It doesn't output the product, ratio or average.

G8B12.why: **Intermodulation** is signals combining in a non-linear circuit to give unwanted outputs.
G8B12.trap: Heterodyning is the same mixing done deliberately.

G8B13.why: Order = sum of multipliers. 2F1−F2 is 2+1 = 3, odd. 3F1−F2 is 4 and 5F1−3F2 is 8, both even.
